**TREASURY MORNING BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype — not an official product*

---

**TOP LINE**
H.R. 7148, the FY2026 consolidated appropriations act, is now law (P.L. 119-75), setting discretionary funding for IRS, FinCEN, OCC, and Departmental Offices. Treasury bureaus must execute appropriated levels and comply with any riders. Ways and Means advanced seven IRS-related bills last cycle; floor scheduling is the next watch item.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Nine Treasury nominees remain stalled. Francis Brooke (Deputy Secretary) has been in referral 56 days. Erin Browne (Under Secretary) sits at 84 days. Sriprakash Kothari (Assistant Secretary) was returned after 184 days. Donald Korb, Jason Trennert, and Luke Petit nominations were withdrawn.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Ways and Means ordered six bills to the floor, including the Taxpayer Workforce Modernization Act (H.R. 7972, 24-16) and ghost preparer regulation (H.R. 9499, 40-0). OFAC published updated Venezuela and Iran general licenses in June. FDTA joint data standards published June 25. North Korea medical device authorization list updated June 11.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee holds FinCEN oversight hearing. Director Andrea Gacki testifies. Staff should monitor questions on beneficial ownership enforcement and sanctions implementation posture.

---

**TOP LINE**
H.R. 7148, the FY2026 consolidated appropriations act, is now law (P.L. 119-75), setting discretionary funding for Treasury, IRS, and FinCEN. Ways and Means advanced six IRS-related bills on strong bipartisan votes. The FinCEN oversight hearing is the primary floor-level Treasury exposure today.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Nine Treasury nominations remain stalled in the Finance Committee pipeline. Deputy Secretary Brooke (55d referred) and Chief Counsel Gadwood (12d) are highest priority. Two nominees were withdrawn; one was returned. No floor votes scheduled.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Ways and Means ordered to report six bills: IRS workforce modernization (H.R. 7972, 24-16), tax-exempt hospital transparency (H.R. 9504, 25-15), hostage tax relief (H.R. 9496, 40-0), Taxpayer Advocate expansion (H.R. 9498, 39-0), fraud victim relief (H.R. 9500, 39-0), AI tax integrity (H.R. 9501, 40-0), and ghost preparer penalties (H.R. 9499, 40-0). Recent Treasury rules updated Venezuela, Iran, and North Korea sanctions general licenses.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee holds FinCEN oversight hearing. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

*Prototype — Public Sources Only — Not an Official Product*

---

**TOP LINE**
FY2026 omnibus (H.R. 7148) is now law, setting Treasury and IRS discretionary funding for the full fiscal year. Ways and Means advanced six IRS-related bills unanimously, signaling fast floor movement. FinCEN Director Gacki faces subcommittee oversight this week.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Nine Treasury nominees remain stalled. Francis Brooke (Deputy Secretary) has sat in committee 54 days. Erin Browne (Under Secretary) at 82 days. Kothari (Asst. Secretary) was returned after 172 days and re-referred. Korb, Trennert, and Petit nominations were withdrawn after delays of 228, 339, and 508 days respectively.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Ways and Means ordered six bills reported, all with strong bipartisan votes: Taxpayer Workforce Modernization Act, Tax Exempt Hospital Transparency Act, Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act, Taxpayer Advocate Participation Act, End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act, AI Tax Integrity Act, and Ghost Preparers Act. Treasury published updated Venezuela, Iran, and North Korea sanctions guidance in June. Financial Data Transparency Act joint data standards also published.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee is conducting oversight of FinCEN. Director Andrea Gacki is the sole witness.

Financial Data Transparency Act joint data standards published June 25.

---

Active Ways and Means referrals include rental housing tax incentives (H.R. 9573), a windfall profits excise tax on major oil companies (H.R. 7960), and retirement savings eligibility expansion (H.R. 4718). Treasury published escrow account lending standards June 29.

Francis Brooke (Deputy Secretary) stalled 52 days. George McMaster (Asst. Secretary) 66 days. Erin Browne (Under Secretary) 80 days. Kothari (Asst. Semiconductor Superiority Act advanced in both chambers (H.R. 8959, S. 4750); Treasury/IRS face Section 48D credit implementation obligations. H.R. 9267 and S. 4657 referred to tax-jurisdiction committees; Office of Tax Policy should assess revenue exposure. H.R. 6556 (Failing Bank Acquisition Fairness Act) placed on Union Calendar; implications for orderly liquidation authority. Recent OFAC actions updated Iran, Venezuela, and North Korea general licenses.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

### Democratic Members — Lines of Questioning and Response Posture

---

## Maxine Waters (D-CA) — Ranking Member

**Line 1 — CTA Rollback / Beneficial Ownership Enforcement**
Waters has consistently framed CTA as a racial and economic justice issue, arguing that shell company secrecy enables predatory lending, money laundering in communities of color, and kleptocrat asset concealment. She is likely to press whether Treasury is actively defending CTA against court challenges and whether FinCEN has the resources and political will to enforce BOI requirements against bad actors, not just small businesses.

**Line 2 — Crypto Illicit Finance and Consumer Harm**
Waters has repeatedly tied crypto to fraud targeting minority communities and unbanked populations. Expect direct questioning on whether Treasury views decentralized finance and unhosted wallets as material AML vulnerabilities, and what concrete rulemaking actions are underway or have been suspended.

**Response Posture**
Lead with concrete enforcement data and rulemaking milestones. Acknowledge litigation constraints without signaling retreat from the statute. Do not invite debate on CTA's constitutional merits. Redirect consumer harm questions toward existing FinCEN guidance and pending rulemakings, noting statutory authority limits where relevant.

---

## Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY)

**Line 1 — Small Business Exemption Scope and Compliance Burden**
Velázquez chairs the Small Business Committee and has raised concerns that BOI reporting requirements disproportionately burden legitimate small and minority-owned businesses while well-resourced bad actors use legal workarounds. She is likely to ask how Treasury calibrated the 20-employee, $5 million revenue exemption thresholds and whether they adequately protect the smallest firms.

**Line 2 — Remittance and Correspondent Banking Pressure on Underserved Communities**
Velázquez has focused on de-risking by large banks that cuts off remittance corridors serving Latino and Caribbean communities. She may ask whether AML modernization efforts include recalibrating risk-based frameworks to prevent over-compliance from choking off legitimate low-dollar transfers.

**Response Posture**
Acknowledge the dual mandate: reduce illicit finance without creating compliance costs that wall off legitimate businesses from the financial system. Cite FinCEN's small business compliance guides and outreach. On de-risking, reference the interagency de-risking statement and note Treasury's willingness to work with the committee on targeted adjustments.

---

## Brad Sherman (D-CA)

**Line 1 — Crypto as a Sanctions Evasion Vehicle**
Sherman is among the most aggressive crypto skeptics in Congress and has introduced legislation to restrict dollar-denominated stablecoins. He is likely to press Treasury on whether current OFAC and FinCEN authorities are sufficient to prevent sanctioned entities, including Russian oligarchs and Iranian actors, from using crypto to circumvent U.S. sanctions, and whether new statutory authority is needed.

**Line 2 — IRS and FinCEN Coordination on Crypto Tax and AML**
Sherman has highlighted gaps between tax reporting and AML reporting for crypto. Expect questions on whether Treasury is coordinating FinCEN and IRS data to identify unreported crypto gains tied to illicit activity, and whether the broker reporting rules finalized under the Inflation Reduction Act are being implemented or quietly deferred.

**Response Posture**
Affirm that OFAC has designated numerous crypto addresses and that Treasury takes sanctions evasion via virtual assets seriously. Cite specific enforcement actions where permissible. On IRS coordination, note existing information-sharing authorities and be precise about what is ongoing versus what requires additional rulemaking. Do not overcommit on statutory requests; redirect to Treasury's legislative priorities.

---

## Gregory W. Meeks (D-NY)

**Line 1 — International AML Standards and FATF Compliance**
Meeks, as former chair of House Foreign Affairs, focuses on the international architecture of anti-money laundering. He is likely to ask whether U.S. implementation of CTA and BOI aligns with FATF Recommendation 24 and whether U.S. grey-listing risk has been reduced by CTA enactment or increased by litigation-driven delays in enforcement.

**Line 2 — Caribbean and African Correspondent Banking De-Risking**
Meeks consistently raises the damage that broad AML compliance pressure does to financial access in Caribbean and African nations. He may ask whether Treasury is actively engaging correspondent banks to maintain relationships with high-risk jurisdictions that are nonetheless making progress on AML reform.

**Response Posture**
Acknowledge that FATF alignment was a core policy rationale for CTA. Note Treasury's engagement with the FATF process and U.S. mutual evaluation timeline. On de-risking, reference Treasury's engagement with affected governments and its coordination with the World Bank and IDB on financial inclusion. Be specific about any ongoing bilateral dialogues.

bills.title: Taxpayer Advocate Participation Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9498 directly affects the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate (OTA) under IRC Section 7803(c) by expanding the National Taxpayer Advocate's participation rights in IRS administrative proceedings. Treasury's implementation risk centers on potential conflicts between OTA advocacy roles and IRS enforcement discretion, as well as resource and procedural demands on the agency if the substitute language broadens statutory intervention triggers.

bills.title: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9500 directly implicates IRS and the Office of Tax Policy, as it would modify tax treatment for victims of fraud-related losses, likely amending IRC sections governing theft loss deductions or income exclusions. The unanimous committee vote signals strong legislative momentum, requiring Treasury and IRS to assess revenue cost, rulemaking obligations, and guidance needs before floor consideration.

bills.title: AI Tax Integrity Act of 2026
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus: Without a known nexus or bill text provided, I cannot reliably identify which specific Treasury office or authority H.R. 9501 touches or characterize its implementation risk. Please supply the bill text or a summary so I can give you an accurate two-sentence brief.

bills.title: Protecting Taxpayers from Ghost Preparers Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9499 would grant IRS authority to regulate and potentially bar "ghost preparers" (those who prepare returns for compensation without signing them), directly implicating the IRS's existing jurisdiction under IRC Section 7407 and Treasury's tax administration oversight role. The implementation risk centers on IRS capacity to build an enforcement and identification infrastructure for an underground preparer population while managing potential litigation over the scope of preparer regulation following the *Loving v. IRS* and *AFTR* decisions.

bills.title: Credit Access and Inclusion Act of 2025
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 28 - 23.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5402 would amend the Fair Credit Reporting Act to allow reporting of on-time utility, telecom, and rental payments to consumer reporting agencies, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Consumer Policy and its work on financial inclusion and credit access. The narrow committee margin (28-23) signals contested implementation questions around data accuracy, consumer dispute rights, and potential disparate impact that Treasury would need to engage on if the bill advances to the floor.

bills.title: Community Flood Resilience Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9056 likely implicates the Federal Insurance Office (FIO) and potentially the Office of Financial Research given their mandates to monitor systemic risk from climate-related financial exposures, including flood risk. Treasury would track implementation demands around data collection, insurance market stability assessments, and any federal backstop or grant mechanisms the bill may authorize.

bills.title: Expressing support for the work of open water lifeguards as first responders and emergency response providers.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
bills.nexus: H.Res. 1188 is a simple expression-of-support resolution with no tax, finance, or appropriations provisions, touching no Treasury office or statutory authority. Treasury has no implementation role, fiscal exposure, or regulatory interest in this measure.

bills.title: Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7960 would impose an excise tax on major integrated oil companies' excess profits, directly implicating IRS's authority to define, assess, and collect a novel excise tax under Title 26. Treasury and IRS face significant implementation risk in establishing a statutory "normal profit" baseline, designing compliance mechanisms for a tax structure with no modern precedent since the 1980 Crude Oil Windfall Profit Tax, and defending against anticipated industry litigation over the tax's constitutional and administrative underpinnings.

bills.title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.nexus: H.R. 7148 directly governs Treasury's annual discretionary funding levels, affecting the operating budgets of the IRS, the Departmental Offices, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), among other bureaus. Implementation risk centers on Treasury's ability to execute congressionally directed spending levels, comply with any accompanying general provisions or riders that restrict or mandate specific agency actions, and avoid Antideficiency Act violations.

bills.title: Helping Young Americans Save for Retirement Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4718 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it would amend retirement savings provisions under the Internal Revenue Code, likely expanding eligibility or contribution rules for younger workers under SECURE 2.0-related authorities. Treasury faces implementation risk in issuing conforming regulations, updating plan qualification guidance, and coordinating with DOL on any parallel ERISA requirements triggered by the Education and Workforce Committee referral.
